examples.text:
[1: Not salsa, not flamenco, my brother. Do you know నాటు ? ]
[2: What is నాటు ? ]
పొలం గట్టు దుమ్ములోన పోట్ల గిత్త దూకినట్టు,
పోలేరమ్మ జాతరలో పోతరాజు ఊగినట్టు,
కిర్రు సెప్పులేసుకుని కర్రసాము సేసినట్టు,
మర్రిసెట్టు నీడలోన కుర్రగుంపు కూడినట్టు,
ఎర్రజొన్న రొట్టెలోన మిరప తొక్కు కలిపినట్టు,
నా పాట సూడు నా పాట సూడు,
నాటు నాటు నాటు నాటు,
నాటు నాటు ఊర నాటు.
examples.ref: 2021, “Naatu Naatu [నాటు నాటు]”, in Chandrabose (lyrics), M. M. Keeravani (music), RRR (soundtrack), performed by Rahul Sipligunj and Kaala Bhairava:
examples.english:
[1: Not salsa, not flamenco, my brother, Do you know నాటు ? ]
[2: What is నాటు ? ]
Like an aggressive bull jumping in the dust of the fields,
Like the lead dancer at the deity Pothuraju’s festival,
Like having a stick battle while wearing wooden sandals,
Like a gang of young boys assembling under the shade of a banyan tree,
Like eating a jowar roti with a chili,
Listen to my song, listen to my song,
Rustic! Rustic! Rustic! Rustic!
Rustic! Rustic! Rustic! Rustic!

polaṁ gaṭṭu dummulōna pōṭla gitta dūkinaṭṭu,

marriseṭṭu nīḍalōna kurragumpu kūḍinaṭṭu,
errajonna roṭṭelōna mirapa tokku kalipinaṭṭu,
nā pāṭa sūḍu nā pāṭa sūḍu,
nāṭu nāṭu nāṭu nāṭu,

Cognate with Tamil அடவி (aṭavi, “forest”), Kannada ಅಡವಿ (aḍavi, “forest”) and Malayalam അടവി (aṭavi, “forest”). Doublet of అటవి (aṭavi).

The personal name, already attested in Eblaite and Ugaritic texts, has been variously translated as "he wrestles with God", "he prevails with God", or "God rules" (possibly from the same root ש־ר־ה/ש־ר־ר as שָׂרָה (“Sarah”)).

etymology_text: From English hot cake in the phrase selling like hot cakes.

examples.english: [The] Russian books are flying off the shelves (lit. "like hot cake").
examples.translation: [The] Russian books are flying off the shelves (lit. "like hot cake").

examples.ref: 2014 June 26, “హాట్ కేకులు.. జనరల్ మెడిసిన్ సీట్లు”, in Eenadu, archived from the original on 10 Jul 2021:
2019 February 27, “టీడీపీ టిక్కెట్ దక్కకపోతే.. పార్టీ మారే అవకాశముంది!”, in Andhra Jyothi, archived from the original on 10 Jul 2021:

examples.text: గతేడాది సాఫ్ట్వేర్ సుధీర్ అంటూ హీరో అయ్యాడు కూడా... ఇక ఇప్పుడు ఈయన డేట్స్ హాట్ కేక్...

examples.translation: "Software" Srinu became a hero last year as well... Now, his dates are hot cake...

etymology_text: From a 2018 interview where Telugu film actor Mohan Babu recalled a dialogue in Telugu where he acted as a villain ordering a hitman to kill his wife and translated it into English; he concluded the dialogue with "Don’t kill so many [sic; actually referring to the number of stabs] like this. Only once. Fasak!", with the last word being an ad-lib that was not present in the original dialogue (possibly being onomatopoeia for chopping or hacking a person). The interview subsequently went viral on the Internet and the word was popularized.

examples.text: ఓన్లీ వన్స్ ఫసక్ అంటూ మోహన్ బాబు చెప్పిన డైలాగును నేర్పించిన బన్నీ..
examples.ref: 2019 September 22, Praveen Kumar Vadla, “మళ్లీ ఇప్పుడు ఫసక్ డైలాగ్ కూతురుతో చెప్పించాడు బన్నీ.”, in News18 Telugu:
examples.english: Once again, he [Allu Arjun] delivered the Finish! dialogue with his daughter.

examples.translation: Once again, he [Allu Arjun] delivered the Finish! dialogue with his daughter.

etymology_text: Compound of కిల్ల (killa, “nipped”) + ఆకు (āku, “leaf”). So called because historically, a leaf indented with marks of the fingernail were sent by a messenger to indicate the reply to a proposal: an odd number of dents for agreement, and an even number for refusal.
